bug_semantics: The advisory characterizes POST /api/v1/invitation-code/redeem as missing authentication because it accepts only an invitation code and returns SDK access and refresh tokens. The first-party design makes the single-use invitation code itself a bearer credential: an authenticated developer generates a code bound server-side to a user, and the standalone mobile app redeems that secret without a second credential. The client cannot choose a user_id at redemption. The implemented code is eight characters sampled with secrets.choice from a 32-character alphabet (32^8 about 1.1 trillion possibilities), expires after seven days, is single-use, and later active codes are revoked when replaced. Redeemed access tokens carry scope sdk. Therefore obtaining and using a valid code is possession of the intended credential, not bypassing an omitted credential; first-use theft of a leaked bearer code remains an inherent bearer-secret risk, not the claimed CWE-287/CWE-306 condition.
flaw_origin: The reported condition originates in the intentional public bearer-code onboarding feature. PR #455 was squash-merged on main as d602dc9f01963e7e7bb9533122dc63368f4d69fd, but its reconstructable first member 8d4ae726e100f72b6687f5a5678f624631c80e8a is the smallest first-writer: it created the public redeem route, valid-code lookup, and SDK access/refresh-token issuance together. Later PR members added replacement-code revocation, tests, a dedicated expiry setting, and documentation; they did not first create the alleged missing-authentication mechanism. The project and CNA subsequently classified the report as a false positive, so there is no security-fix commit.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first review does not validate the advisory's premise. Redemption is deliberately passwordless but not credentialless: the random, expiring, single-use, server-bound invitation code is the authentication factor, and an attacker who has a valid code has acquired that bearer credential. The original feature request, specification, route docstring, and maintainer disposition agree on this trust model; the CNA then rejected the CVE as not a security issue. The lifecycle is introduction in decomposed member 8d4ae726e100f72b6687f5a5678f624631c80e8a, squash landing d602dc9f01963e7e7bb9533122dc63368f4d69fd, first release 0.3.0-beta, continued presence through 0.7.0 and HEAD, report/clarification, and administrative rejection without a code fix or patched release. AI judgment is nevertheless made solely from the true BIC object: its human author/committer identity and trailer-free message provide no AI evidence, so NOT_AI is the supported verdict.
remaining_gap: No evidentiary gap remains. The case is intentionally unpatched: fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are null because the endpoint remains by design, the maintainer closed the report as a false positive, and the CNA rejected CVE-2026-78154 rather than assigning a patched version.
